findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, it is passed verbatim to `/bin/sh`. For example, `main; attacker-command` executes the second command with the application's privileges rather than treating the input as a Git revision. Valid refs containing metacharacters such as `&` also change behavior. Preserve argv-based execution with `execFile` or an equivalent non-shell API.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve argv-based execution for branches containing shell metacharacters
findings.body:
Valid Git branch names may contain `&`. On POSIX, `showBranch("topic&wait")` becomes `git show topic & wait`, launching the wrong Git command asynchronously and returning the shell’s status rather than showing `topic&wait`; it can even report success with empty output.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` verbatim, introducing arbitrary command execution wherever callers pass untrusted input. On POSIX, `showBranch("main; attacker-command")` executes `attacker-command` with the application’s privileges; the previous `execFile` implementation treated the value only as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names as argv instead of executing them through a shell
findings.body:
On POSIX, valid Git ref names can contain shell metacharacters. For example, `topic;sleep${IFS}20` passes `git check-ref-format` but causes `showBranch()` to spawn `sleep` rather than pass the complete ref to Git. Repeated or crafted inputs can launch long-lived, high-CPU, or high-output processes and exhaust process, memory, or I/O resources. `execFile` avoided shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve the branch argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, so a branch such as `main; id` executes an additional command with the process’s privileges. It also breaks valid refs containing shell metacharacters: this repository contains `refs/heads/topic&wait`, which `execFile` passed as one argument, while the new implementation parses `&` as a shell operator.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
